sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 7.7% a year from FY2018 to FY2025, reaching $25.8 billion [F145][F8].
The path was a step change rather than a smooth climb: revenue jumped 22.3% in FY2022 and then fell 5.2% in FY2024 [D131][D201].
The FY2024 decline came from lower storm cost recovery revenues of about $1,090 million and lower fuel cost recovery revenues of about $526 million [P34].
Operating income swung from a 15.5% margin in FY2021 to 41.3% in FY2023, a 23.5pp change, as the prior years carried large equity-method impairments [F20][F22][D177][P68].
FPL remains the core, at 70.5% of FY2025 revenue, and contributed 5.5pp of the 9.8% revenue growth that year [D271][D273][D236].
FPL's FY2025 revenue rose $1,243 million on higher storm cost recovery, retail base and storm protection plan cost recovery revenues, partly offset by lower fuel cost recovery [P21].
Operating costs grew 0.2pp faster than revenue in FY2025, at 10.0% [D257][D249].
Operating income still grew 10.7% against revenue growth of 9.8%, an incremental margin of 34.8% [D237][D236][D256].
Net income fell 1.6% while diluted EPS fell 2.1% as the diluted share count rose 0.6% [D238][D240][D251].
The FY2025 operating margin of 32.1% sits above the 30.3% window median but well below the 41.3% FY2023 high [F24][D300][D299].
D&A rose to 25.5% of revenue in FY2025, up from 23.2%, as depreciation and amortization expense increased $951 million on higher storm cost amortization and plant in service [D224][D189][P16].
In FY2025 net margin of 26.5% sat 5.6pp below the 32.1% operating margin [F40][F24][D327].
The gap reflects a -17.7% effective tax rate and $3,750 million of other expense, with Corporate and Other hurt by non-qualifying hedge activity and higher debt balances [D226][X64][P8].
Operating cash flow of $12,485 million was 1.83x net income in FY2025, below the 1.95x window median [F64][F32][D227][D319].
Operating cash flow fell 5.8% while net income fell 1.6% [D241][D238].
The swing from net over-recovery to net under-recovery of cost recovery clauses cut FPL's operating cash flow by about $89 million [P19].
Investing outflow of $23,865 million dwarfed operating cash flow, and D&A of $6,580 million covered only part of that capital spend [F72][F64][X32].
Net debt reached $92.2 billion in FY2025, or net cash of -357.4% of revenue [D231][D232].
That is deeper than the -235.4% utilities peer median and ranks in the 0th percentile of the three-peer group [D329][D328].
Long-term debt rose 23.7% to $89,556 million while total debt grew 15.7% [D245][F136][D253].
Dividends of $4,680 million were funded alongside $23,394 million of new debt issuance, and the diluted share count still rose 0.6% [X82][X90][D251].
The current ratio was 0.60x in FY2025, below 1.0x, though it is the window high [F128][D305].
For a regulated utility with committed credit lines this is a working-capital convention rather than a liquidity crisis, but it leaves little short-term cushion [F128].
Net debt rose for a seventh straight year, from $34.3 billion in FY2018 to $92.2 billion in FY2025 [D9][D231][R2].
The steady debt-funded build is the central balance-sheet risk, and the 0th-percentile net cash position shows how far it sits from peers [D328].
The effective tax rate moved -23.3pp to -17.7% in FY2025, driven by clean energy tax credits that rose about $585 million [D226][D191][P11].
A negative tax rate flatters net income, so the 26.5% net margin overstates underlying earning power [F40].
Whether the FY2026 operating margin holds above the 30.3% window median, after 32.1% in FY2025, in the next 10-K [F24][D300].
Whether net cash as a share of revenue improves from -357.4% in FY2025 toward the -235.4% peer median [D232][D329].
Whether operating cash flow to net income recovers from 1.83x toward the 1.95x window median [D227][D319].
